attributionInventory.purpose: Volume VII describes the other eight volumes in Part I, Part II, Part III, and the Coda. Each description is checked against the restored reality of the volume it names. Volume III let the idea expand: holds against Volume III's restored shape.
Volume IV gave the expansion a structure: holds against Volume IV's architecture volume.
Volume V returned the measure to the human: holds; Volume V is the human-return volume by its own sections, including On Returning to the Human.

Volume VI reduced the whole toward its simplest, most elegant form: holds; Volume VIII independently describes the sixth as the simplest and most elegant statement, and Volume VI carries the current figure this volume builds on.

Volume VIII carries Saturn, limits, time, and the hard accounting: holds; Volume VIII names Saturn as its governing figure in its own headings and bounds the symbolism exactly as VII's Part II head disclaimer does.
Volume IX returns to the ground and asks what can be built: holds; Volume VIII closes by saying Volume IX asks what can be built, and Volume IX's restored text answers to it.

phantoms.claim: In the second we turned to the space between things, and found there the thing itself: intelligence, not the property of any single mind, but the pattern that connects, the relatedness in which meaning is born.
phantoms.reality: Volume II's restored manuscript contains none of it: no space between things, no pattern that connects, no relatedness. Its actual matter is the crisis beneath the crises, the nervous system as civilizational ground, relational coherence, the architecture of extraction, and coherence as infrastructure. The pattern which connects lives in Volume VI, The Between, with its Bateson and Buhner attribution. This is the known intelligence-ontology phantom family P3.
